object_description: T-shaped building composition with expressive sports cube
design_condition: The building sets its longitudinal structure back from the street, forms a small courtyard, and uses a raised sports volume to create a strong urban figure beside the neighbouring buildings.

positive.statement: The project proposes a remarkably idiosyncratic composition of perpendicular wall panels and two fields.

position.target: perpendicular wall panels and two fields
position.rationale: Top view shows perpendicular fields and elevations confirm their layered volumetric composition.

positive.statement: The expressive sports figure gains enough strength for the relatively small building to assert itself independently in the urban space.

position.rationale: Distinctive raised sports volume is concentrated at the southwest end of the footprint.

positive.statement: The setbacks and contrasting building shapes nevertheless create volumetric unity.

position.rationale: Distributed marker captures the stepped setbacks and contrasting masses across the building.

positive.statement: The atrium and central organization create surprisingly new spatial experiences within a familiar corridor arrangement.

position.rationale: Top view indicates a central courtyard-like void within the surrounding corridor arrangement.

positive.statement: The school wing structure is functional, efficient, and easy to implement.

position.rationale: School wing is approximated along the long eastern building arm.

positive.statement: The project achieves a strong urban-development response and a spatially convincing school proposal.

position.rationale: Broad marker covers the visible school mass and its urban-facing spatial response.

negative.statement: The small courtyard and differentiated planting, lounge, and hedge areas are unlikely to be robust enough for the site.

position.target: small courtyard and differentiated planting, lounge, and hedge areas
position.rationale: Small southwest courtyard edge is the plausible location for planting and landscape subdivisions.

negative.statement: The courtyard is hardly suitable as a publicly usable neighbourhood space.

position.rationale: Central-south open space is approximated from the visible footprint gap.

negative.statement: The open arrangement of the kiosk is an operational disadvantage.

position.rationale: Kiosk is not distinguishable; constrained near the likely public-facing southwest frontage.

negative.statement: The classroom dimensions are at the lower limit and the exposed collections restrict usability and flexibility.

position.rationale: Interior classrooms are unexposed, so the long school wing provides the constrained anchor.

negative.statement: The front glazing of the gymnasiums and the equipment-room design may restrict sports use.

position.target: front glazing of the gymnasiums and equipment-room design
position.rationale: Southwest sports volume is the likely gymnasium frontage and equipment-support location.

negative.statement: The sports supporting structure is not convincing conceptually or technically, particularly because of deformation and vibration behaviour.

position.rationale: Raised sports volume provides the only visible anchor for its supporting structure.

negative.statement: The very large sports-hall windows increase cooling demand and the risk of summer overheating.

position.rationale: South-facing edge of the raised sports volume is the constrained window location.

negative.statement: The building violates the applicable building regulations despite moving away from the construction line.

position.rationale: South site edge approximates the referenced construction-line relationship.

negative.statement: The below-average space efficiency, oversized basement, and atrium fire-protection requirements lead to poor economic efficiency.

position.rationale: Judgment concerns combined cost, efficiency, basement, and fire-protection performance.
